source.summary: Server-side EQEmu multiclass audit for Heroes Journey style rebuild.
source.primary_goal: Implement 1/2/3-class characters while preserving one primary/display class for client compatibility.

defaults.review_expectation: implementation only; do not perform unrelated refactors
testing_expectation: Build affected EQEmu server targets where practical.
Run focused regression/manual tests listed in each slice.

queue.title: Add schema and runtime assigned-class set
queue.objective: Persist up to three assigned classes per character without changing client-facing packet layouts.
context: Keep character_data.class_ as the primary/display class.
Add class_2 and class_3 as nullable/optional secondary and tertiary assigned-class slots.
Existing single-class characters must load/save unchanged.
Do not widen player profile, char select, name approval, or spawn packet structs.
implementation_notes: Add DB migration for character_data.class_2 and character_data.class_3.
Regenerate or update the character_data repository layer after migration.
Load assigned classes into a server-side runtime container, normalizing invalid/duplicate/empty slots.
Primary/display class must always be included in the assigned-class set.
Use max 3 assigned classes.
Prefer simple columns for this initial implementation because the code already loads one character_data row and clients only expose one visible class.
acceptance_criteria: Existing characters without class_2/class_3 load and save unchanged.
A two-class character round-trips through DB load/save.
A three-class character round-trips through DB load/save.
Invalid duplicate class slots are rejected or normalized deterministically.
Char select still shows only character_data.class_.
tests: Create/load/save stock single-class character.
Manually set class_2/class_3 in DB and verify runtime assigned-class set after login.
Zone/relog and verify values persist.
Verify no packet struct layout changes were made.
risks: Repository regeneration may be required.
Migration ordering can break fresh installs if not added in the expected EQEmu style.
Hidden assumptions may treat class_ as mutable runtime authority.

queue.title: Introduce central multiclass helper layer
queue.objective: Create one canonical helper surface for assigned-class membership, skill caps, AA gating, and spell level lookup.
context: Avoid scattered GetClass() replacement work without a central API.
Default Mob behavior should remain single-class.
Client-specific behavior should consult the assigned-class set.
implementation_notes: Add helpers such as GetAssignedClasses(), HasAssignedClass(uint8 class_id), GetEffectiveSkillCap(skill_id), GetLowestAssignedSpellLevel(spell_id), and CanUseAAForAssignedClasses(...).
Keep helper names and signatures simple and easy to grep.
Mob base implementation should return the existing single class.
Client override should use the loaded assigned-class set.
Helpers should preserve exact stock behavior when only one assigned class exists.
Do not alter item restrictions, faction, titles, who list, or visible class semantics in this slice.
acceptance_criteria: Assigned-class helper API compiles and is available to skill, AA, and spell paths.
Single-class helper outputs match current GetClass()-based behavior.
Multiclass helper outputs are deterministic and max three classes.
No packet struct changes.
tests: Add focused unit-style or debug checks where EQEmu test harness allows.
Manual GM/debug verification for one-, two-, and three-class assigned sets.
Build affected zone/common targets.
risks: Helper signatures may need adjustment once AA/spell call sites are touched.
Missed direct GetClass() gates can create partial multiclass behavior.

queue.title: Refactor skill caps to use highest assigned-class cap
queue.objective: Make regular skills use the highest cap available from any assigned class.
context: Examples: Paladin + Monk + Necromancer should receive the best applicable defensive, avoidance, and casting skill caps among the assigned classes.
Single-class characters must remain stock-compatible.
implementation_notes: Implement effective skill cap as max cap across assigned classes.
Update CanHaveSkill(), MaxSkill(), GetSkillTrainLevel(), MaxSkills(), CheckIncreaseSkill(), ShowSkillsWindow(), and starting skill initialization as needed.
Fix the reported GetSkillTrainLevel() loop/key issue if confirmed during implementation.
Avoid broad unrelated refactors.
Keep display class untouched.
acceptance_criteria: Single-class skill caps match stock EQEmu.
Two-/three-class characters receive max cap across assigned classes for each skill.
Paladin + Monk + Necromancer test case produces expected best-of-class caps.
GM skill tools reflect effective multiclass caps.
Skill increases do not exceed effective multiclass cap.
tests: Compare single-class caps before/after for representative classes.
Test Paladin+Monk+Necromancer defense/dodge/block/casting caps.
Use #set skill_all_max and #showskills to verify max values.
Level character and verify MaxSkills behavior.
risks: Training level and skill cap behavior may differ by client/era.
Starting skills may need separate treatment from max caps.
Confirmed bug fix in common/skill_caps.cpp could affect stock behavior if not scoped carefully.

queue.title: Union AA eligibility across assigned classes
queue.objective: Allow a character to view, purchase, load, save, and use AA abilities available to any assigned class without duplicating AA state.
context: AA ownership/state remains one per character.
Do not split character_alternate_abilities rows by class.
Replace single-class bitmask checks with any-assigned-class helper checks.
implementation_notes: Update CanUseAlternateAdvancementRank(), CanPurchaseAlternateAdvancementRank(), SendAlternateAdvancementRank(), LoadAlternateAdvancement(), SaveAA(), GrantAlternateAdvancementAbility(), PurchaseAlternateAdvancementRank(), and TogglePassiveAlternativeAdvancement() where class gating applies.
Preserve one aa_ranks map per character.
Ensure grant-only and passive AA handling still works.
Keep primary/display class for client-visible identity.
acceptance_criteria: Single-class AA list/purchase/use behavior remains stock-compatible.
Multiclass character can see eligible AAs from any assigned class.
Multiclass character can purchase and activate eligible AAs from any assigned class.
AA load/save remains one state record per character.
No duplicate AA state by class is introduced.
tests: Create single-class regression test for AA purchase/use.
Use #set aa_points and #grantaa on multiclass character.
Verify AA list includes abilities from each assigned class.
Relog and verify purchased AAs persist once.
risks: Grant-only AA edge cases.
Titanium/older-client AA display differences.
AA ranks with class assumptions outside simple class bitmasks.

queue.title: Share spell and discipline access across assigned classes
queue.objective: Allow spells/disciplines from any assigned class and use the lowest spell level requirement among assigned classes.
context: Spellbook and memmed-spell persistence remain per character.
If Paladin and Cleric both receive a heal, Paladin+Cleric should use the Cleric level requirement when Cleric receives it earlier.
Global minimum spell level across all classes is not sufficient; helper must be character-scoped to assigned classes.
implementation_notes: Update scribing, discipline learning, spellbook access, memorization/casting gates, fizzle checks, spell group cache behavior, and spell-effect level limits where class/level gates apply.
Implement character-scoped lowest assigned spell level helper.
Do not rely only on common/spdat.cpp::GetSpellMinimumLevel(), because that is global across all classes.
Keep character_spells and character_memmed_spells unchanged.
Watch older-client spellbook limits and translator clipping behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Single-class spell access remains stock-compatible.
Multiclass character can scribe/learn spells or disciplines from any assigned class.
Shared spells use the lowest required level among assigned classes, not global minimum across all classes.
Paladin+Cleric shared heal test uses Cleric level if Cleric gets it earlier.
Spell casting validation agrees with scribing/learning eligibility.
No spellbook/memmed-spell schema split by class.
tests: Single-class scribe/cast regression.
Paladin+Cleric shared heal level test.
Hybrid caster + pure caster spell level comparison.
Discipline learning test for melee assigned class.
Relog and verify spellbook persistence.
Check older-client spellbook capacity behavior where practical.
risks: Spell group cache query may embed single-class assumptions.
Older clients may clip large spellbooks.
Spell effects may have class/level gates separate from normal cast checks.

queue.title: Preserve visible-class compatibility and add GM multiclass tooling
queue.objective: Keep client-visible class behavior stable while giving admins a clean way to assign and verify multiclass data.
context: Client packets expose exactly one class.
Primary/display class should remain stable for char select, who list, titles, faction, item restrictions, and similar UI-facing paths.
This slice is compatibility and operator tooling, not broad gameplay expansion.
implementation_notes: Confirm char select, name approval, spawn/profile, who list, titles, faction, and item restrictions still use primary/display class only.
Add GM command or quest hook to assign class_2/class_3 and display assigned-class set.
Do not widen packet structs.
Add clear validation: max three classes, primary class required, no duplicates, valid class IDs only.
Document intended display-class vs assigned-class split in code comments or docs.
acceptance_criteria: Char select and zoning remain client-compatible.
Visible/display class remains character_data.class_.
GM/admin can assign, clear, and inspect secondary/tertiary classes.
Invalid multiclass assignments are rejected with clear messages.
Item restrictions, faction, titles, and who list remain primary-class based unless explicitly changed later.
tests: Verify char select shows primary class only.
Verify /who or equivalent visible class behavior remains primary class.
Use GM command/hook to set Paladin+Monk+Necromancer and inspect assigned classes.
Try duplicate/invalid class assignments and verify rejection.
Zone/relog after GM changes and verify persistence.
risks: Accidental packet layout changes can break clients.
Operators may expect visible class to show multiclass data; document that this is intentionally server-side for now.
GM command naming may collide with existing command conventions.

queue.title: End-to-end multiclass regression pass
queue.objective: Validate the complete server-side multiclass feature against representative class combinations and stock single-class behavior.
context: This is a focused validation/remediation slice after core implementation lands.
Do not add new feature scope unless required to fix regressions from MC-001 through MC-006.
files_to_inspect_or_change: GM command files touched by earlier slices
implementation_notes: Create a concise manual test matrix for one-, two-, and three-class characters.
Exercise at least one tank/melee/caster trio, one priest/hybrid shared-spell pair, and one pure single-class regression.
Patch only confirmed regressions caused by multiclass changes.
Capture any remaining out-of-scope findings as future backlog candidates.
acceptance_criteria: Single-class regression matrix passes.
Paladin+Monk+Necromancer skill cap matrix passes.
Paladin+Cleric shared spell level matrix passes.
AA union purchase/use matrix passes.
Char select/zoning compatibility remains intact.
Any remaining known limitations are documented.
tests: Single class: baseline skill, AA, spell behavior.
Two class: Paladin+Cleric spell sharing and AA visibility.
Three class: Paladin+Monk+Necromancer skill caps and mixed spell/AA access.
Relog and zoning persistence checks.
Older-client spellbook capacity smoke test where practical.
risks: Some EQEmu behavior may require live/manual validation instead of automated tests.
Large spellbooks may expose client-era limits.
Edge cases may emerge in class-specific spell effects or AA restrictions.

future_candidates.title: Multiclass-aware item restrictions
future_candidates.reason: Deferred to keep initial implementation client-safe and avoid UI/game-balance ambiguity.

future_candidates.title: Multiclass-aware titles/faction/who display
future_candidates.reason: Deferred because client-visible systems expose one class and should remain display-class based initially.

future_candidates.title: Player-facing multiclass selection UI or quest flow
future_candidates.reason: Initial scope should use GM/quest hooks for validation before building user-facing flows.

future_candidates.title: Bot/merc multiclass support audit
future_candidates.reason: Audit notes bot/merc class paths are separate and should be handled independently later.
